newsitem.title: CANADA: Rio Algom credits Q2 gain to copper price.
newsitem.headline: Rio Algom credits Q2 gain to copper price.

text.p: Rio Algom Ltd said on Wednesday said a 36 percent increase in second quarter net income was due mainly to higher copper prices.
Rio Algom reported a C$28 million profit in the three months ended June 30, up from C$20.7 million in the same period a year ago.
The spot London Metal Exchange price for copper averaged US$1.14 per pound during the quarter, up two percent from the second quarter of 1996.

"The continued strength in copper prices has certainly been good news, but I am also pleased by our operational progress," Rio Algom president and chief executive officer Pat James said in a statement.

Cash costs at the Cerro Colorado mine in Chile were down 15 percent in the second quarter from the same period a year earlier. Operating costs at metals unit Vincent Metal Goods have also declined, James said.
The average cash cost for production in the second quarter was US$0.58 per pound, down slightly from US$0.59 in the same quarter last year.

Copper production in the quarter fell to 61.7 million pounds from 63.1 million pounds in the second quarter of 1996. The decline was due to lower production at the Highland Valley mine in British Columbia.
